_comment: ORDER-602 A (rescoped after Codex audit 8). ATTESTATION log for the S2a proposal -- an append-only record that a decision was WRITTEN DOWN against specific bytes. It is NOT proof of who made it: this repository commits under a single git identity, so nothing here separates the owner from any other writer, and the earlier name 'sign-off' overclaimed. Do not cite it as a signature. WHAT IT STILL BUYS: recording a decision no longer means editing the evidence, the acceptance rule and the generator in one commit -- C2 keeps refusing APPROVED inside D1, and the decision is written here instead. THE OWNER WRITES HERE and nothing else changes. Append one object per decision; never edit or delete a previous line -- that is enforced (A7): the version committed at HEAD must remain a byte prefix of this file. Required: bundle_sha256, current_owner, decision (APPROVED|REFUSED), signer, decided_at, reason. bundle_sha256 covers D1 + D2 + the coverage reconciliation + the generator + both validators, so a change to the reviewed document or to the acceptance rules invalidates the record rather than silently reinterpreting it. The latest line per current_owner wins. Run check_s2a_attestation.py --template for a ready-made line with the current digest filled in.

reason: Coverage transfer approved (MASTER_BACKLOG.md section 2 -> factory/coverage.jsonl), CONDITIONAL on two things S2 must honour: (1) the owner banner and the section-2 header must say 'generated from factory/coverage.jsonl; edits here are overwritten' in the SAME commit as the first generation -- nothing machine-reads section 2 today, so the only real risk is a human trusting the old banner and hand-editing generated output; (2) section 2 must NOT be switched to generated output until factory/coverage.jsonl covers at least what the current hand table covers -- the present 7 rows are stale (last real update 2026-06-27 against a 64-row deployment inventory) but they are not nothing, and a thinner generated table would be a regression. Decision basis: measured, not assumed -- the only parser of the section-2 heading in the repo is this order's own checker, and scripts/check_state.ps1:124 opens the file solely to assert its owner-banner line.

reason: Third re-record, and the reason is structural rather than a change of mind: check_s2a_attestation.py is inside its own bundle, so every repair to it moves the digest and voids the record that authorised the previous repair. Digest history this session: aaa5998d -> 1bd4d268 -> fa6bab35 -> 6ec25ca5. This one follows a /scrutinize finding that `latest` was built from every row including malformed ones, so appending one bad line demoted the real decision to superseded and let it skip A2 and A6 (under-reporting, not a green bypass -- A1 still reddened the log). Owner's confirmation, verbatim: 'yeun-yan, chai mai yak khoi yeun-yan man sia wela, kae loei' -- confirmed, and asked for the repeated-signing itself to be fixed. That is ORDER-614; it costs ONE more signature to land and none afterwards. NOTE: line 4 is NOT edited or removed -- it is superseded, which is the exact D1 mechanism approved in line 4 itself, working.

reason: Fourth re-record. ORDER-615 batch B landed five repairs to check_s2a_attestation.py in ONE commit rather than five, so this is one signature where the previous session spent four. Digest history: aaa5998d -> 1bd4d268 -> fa6bab35 -> 6ec25ca5 -> 7616f2de. The repairs: A7 now judges the STAGED bytes rather than the working tree (a commit could otherwise rewrite append-only history with the gate green); expected_post_state may only bind the file the record decides for, and rejects a missing path or a directory tree-oid; a non-object JSON line is reported instead of crashing the loader; and a failed in-force row no longer lets the superseded row be reported as the current decision. None of these changes what is DEMANDED of a record -- they change what is correctly READ. Owner's confirmation, verbatim: 'yeun-yan' after being shown this digest and that the decision itself is unchanged. ORDER-614 rev 2 is the order that ends this signature loop: policy plus conformance vectors, implementation outside the bundle.
